description: A Distributed Denial of Service attack floods a target with traffic from many sources simultaneously, exhausting network bandwidth or server resources so legitimate users cannot connect. Traffic typically shows a sudden spike in connection volume from many distinct source IPs, often with abnormally small or repetitive packet patterns.
detection_indicators: Sudden sharp increase in flow volume / packets per second
Traffic originating from an unusually large number of distinct source IPs
Low per-connection duration with high connection rate
mitigation: Enable rate limiting and traffic filtering at the network edge / load balancer
Use a DDoS protection service (cloud-based scrubbing) to absorb volumetric traffic
Configure auto-scaling so legitimate capacity isn't exhausted
Blackhole or null-route traffic from confirmed malicious source ranges

description: HULK (HTTP Unbearable Load King) is an application-layer DoS tool that generates a high volume of unique, obfuscated HTTP GET requests to a web server, aiming to bypass caching and exhaust server resources with a single or few source hosts rather than a distributed swarm.
detection_indicators: High request rate to a single web endpoint from one or few source IPs
Unusually varied/randomized request parameters designed to defeat caching
Elevated server CPU/connection load with normal-looking individual requests
mitigation: Deploy a Web Application Firewall (WAF) with rate-based rules
Enable connection/request rate limiting per source IP
Use CAPTCHA or challenge-response for suspicious high-rate clients

description: GoldenEye is an HTTP DoS tool that keeps many connections open using KeepAlive plus Cache-Control headers, exhausting the web server's available connection pool rather than saturating bandwidth.
detection_indicators: Large number of long-lived, low-activity HTTP connections
Server connection pool exhaustion despite modest bandwidth usage
mitigation: Limit maximum concurrent connections per client IP
Reduce KeepAlive timeout on the web server
Deploy a reverse proxy / WAF to absorb and filter connections

description: Slowloris opens many connections to a web server and sends partial HTTP requests very slowly, keeping connections open indefinitely to exhaust the server's connection pool with minimal bandwidth.
detection_indicators: Many connections stuck in a partially-open / incomplete-request state
Very low data throughput per connection over a long connection duration
mitigation: Set aggressive timeouts for incomplete HTTP requests
Use a reverse proxy (e.g. nginx) which handles slow clients more gracefully than some servers
Limit concurrent connections per source IP

description: Slowhttptest is a tool for simulating slow-rate application-layer DoS attacks (including Slowloris-style and slow POST body attacks), sending data at an artificially low rate to hold connections open.
detection_indicators: Abnormally low data transfer rate sustained over long connection durations
High ratio of open connections to actual completed requests
mitigation: Enforce minimum data rate thresholds, dropping connections that fall below it
Use request timeout and body-size limits at the web server / WAF layer

description: Port scanning is reconnaissance activity where an attacker probes a range of ports on a target host to discover open services, often a precursor to a targeted exploit attempt.
detection_indicators: Many connection attempts to different ports on the same destination host in a short time
High proportion of failed/reset connections (closed ports)
Sequential or patterned port access order
mitigation: Deploy an Intrusion Detection/Prevention System (IDS/IPS) tuned for scan signatures
Use firewall rules to restrict exposed ports to only what's needed
Rate-limit or temporarily block source IPs showing scan-like behavior

description: Patator (FTP module) performs automated brute-force login attempts against an FTP server, systematically trying many username/password combinations.
detection_indicators: High volume of failed authentication attempts against FTP in a short window
Repeated login attempts from the same source IP to the same account
mitigation: Enforce account lockout / exponential backoff after repeated failed logins
Require strong passwords and, where possible, key-based authentication instead of passwords
Restrict FTP access via IP allowlisting or VPN

description: Patator (SSH module) performs automated brute-force login attempts against an SSH server, systematically trying many credential combinations.
detection_indicators: High volume of failed SSH authentication attempts in a short window
Repeated connection attempts from the same source targeting SSH (port 22)
mitigation: Disable password authentication in favor of SSH key-based auth
Use fail2ban or similar tools to auto-block IPs after repeated failures
Move SSH to a non-default port and/or restrict via allowlist/VPN

description: Automated attempts to guess valid login credentials on a web application's authentication endpoint by systematically trying many username/password combinations.
detection_indicators: High rate of failed login POST requests to the same endpoint
Many distinct username/password combinations tried from the same source in a short time
mitigation: Implement account lockout, CAPTCHA, or rate limiting on login endpoints
Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA)
Monitor and alert on abnormal failed-login spikes

mitre_technique_name: Cross-Site Scripting (via Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript)
description: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) injects malicious script into web pages viewed by other users, typically via unsanitized input fields, to steal session data, hijack accounts, or perform actions as the victim.
detection_indicators: HTTP requests containing script tags or JavaScript event handlers in parameters
Unusual characters (<, >, script keywords) in form fields or URL parameters
mitigation: Sanitize and encode all user-supplied input before rendering in HTML
Apply a Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict script execution sources
Use a Web Application Firewall with XSS-pattern detection rules

description: Botnet traffic indicates a compromised host communicating with a command-and-control (C2) server, receiving instructions or exfiltrating data, often as part of a larger coordinated attack infrastructure.
detection_indicators: Periodic, regularly-timed 'beaconing' connections to a small set of external hosts
Traffic to known-bad or newly-registered domains/IPs
Unusual protocol usage inconsistent with the host's normal role
mitigation: Isolate and reimage confirmed infected hosts
Block C2 domains/IPs at the DNS or firewall layer using threat intelligence feeds
Deploy endpoint detection and response (EDR) to catch beaconing behavior

description: This category groups several very low-frequency attack types from the dataset (Infiltration, Heartbleed exploitation, SQL Injection) that had too few examples to model reliably on their own. Infiltration (T1190) involves exploiting a public-facing application to gain internal network access; Heartbleed exploits a TLS/OpenSSL vulnerability (CVE-2014-0160) to leak memory contents; SQL Injection (T1190) injects malicious SQL via unsanitized input to manipulate a backend database.
detection_indicators: Anomalous internal network access following an external-facing service interaction
TLS heartbeat requests with mismatched length fields (Heartbleed signature)
SQL syntax or injection patterns in web request parameters
mitigation: Patch and update all public-facing software and TLS libraries promptly
Use parameterized queries / prepared statements to prevent SQL injection
Segment networks so a compromised public-facing service has limited internal reach
